## Task lifecycle

- A qualifying operation may return a durable task handle when the tasks extension is negotiated.
- tasks/get polls authoritative status, bounded progress, result, error, expiration, and recovery.
- tasks/update supplies mid-flight client input and composes with MRTR without two conflicting state machines.
- Cancellation and timeout are idempotent and terminal task states are immutable events.
- Handles are scoped to workspace, authority, protocol policy, and retention; they never expose filesystem paths or secrets.
- Existing pm plan, test-run, telemetry, and history identifiers remain domain records and are not silently conflated with transport task handles.
Official MCP tasks extension for pm: asynchronous long operations, tasks/get polling, tasks/update input, durable handles, and lifecycle convergence
Expose long-running pm operations through io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks with SDK-owned durable handles, polling, mid-flight input, cancellation, expiration, and immutable lifecycle evidence.

The tasks extension is explicitly negotiated and never appears as an unadvertised core capability; Eligible long operations can return durable handles without per-request opt-in and tasks/get reports bounded authoritative state; tasks/update accepts validated mid-flight input and composes deterministically with MRTR inputResponses; tasks/list and blocking tasks/result are not implemented on the canonical 2026-07-28 path; Cancellation, duplicate updates, expiration, unauthorized access, restart recovery, retention, and immutable terminal evidence have negative tests; The SDK provides a transport-neutral task provider and adapters for test, reindex, graph, import, and validation operations
Standard asynchronous execution for long pm operations
Map tests, reindexing, graph analysis, imports, validation, and other bounded long operations onto the official tasks extension
Hosts can start, inspect, steer, cancel, and recover long pm work without blocking a request or inventing a private job protocol
2026-07-28 moves tasks out of core and redesigns them around tasks/get, tasks/update, unsolicited handles, and extension negotiation
